source_note: Portal counts: City of Chicago Data Portal, Crimes - 2001 to Present (ijzp-q8t2), https://data.cityofchicago.org/Public-Safety/Crimes-2001-to-Present/ijzp-q8t2 , queried via SoQL 2026-10-05; latest record date 2026-09-27 (max updated_on 2026-10-04). Counts are reported incidents by primary_type (one row per incident/offence, not per victim; 'ALL' = all primary types). Portal data are preliminary, exclude some records (e.g. sealed/expunged, murders reclassified), lag, and are revised; CPD press-release figures use different definitions (Part I index crimes, homicide victims) so numbers will not match exactly (e.g. 2025 homicides: CPD 416 vs portal 440; 2024: CPD 587 vs portal 597). CPD 2025-in-review PDF: https://www.chicagopolice.org/wp-content/uploads/2025-in-Review.pdf (preliminary, subject to change). Web-page figures were extracted by a summarising fetch tool; key numbers cross-checked where noted.
scope_warning: Citywide figures cover all of Chicago, ~230 sq mi, and are dominated by South/West Side violence that rarely touches tourists; Districts 1 (Central: Loop, South Loop, Millennium Park) and 18 (Near North: Magnificent Mile, River North, Streeterville, Gold Coast, Old Town) are the visitor areas but also host the highest property-crime counts because of huge daytime/visitor populations (rates per resident are meaningless/inflated there). Per-100k district rates are NOT VERIFIED (no official district residential population sourced). Not a prediction of risk for any individual.

ytd_2026_vs_2025.source: Data Portal SoQL, 2026-10-05; preliminary; recent weeks under-reported (lag)
ytd_2026_vs_2025.district_note: District figures are incident counts, not rates; ward/district residential population NOT VERIFIED. Counts for D1/D18 include visitor-driven theft.
ytd_2026_vs_2025.anomaly_warning: Burglary (+50.6% citywide, +90.7% D1, +57.0% D18) and motor vehicle theft (+8.4% citywide, +28.3% D18) rise sharply while almost everything else falls; 2026 YTD burglary (10,346) already exceeds full-year 2025 (9,740). Possible recording/reclassification change or data artefact: cause NOT VERIFIED; do not publish as a real surge without CPD confirmation.

millennium_park_minor_policy.rule: Guests under 18 must be accompanied by an adult aged 21+ after 6 p.m., Friday through Sunday; ID may be requested; adult must stay for whole visit and may escort up to four young people. Park open daily 6am-11pm; Fri-Sun 4-11pm only the Michigan Ave/Washington St and Michigan/Madison entrances open, with security wanding and bag check. Tree Lighting Ceremony listed for Friday 20 Nov 2026 (no outside alcohol).
millennium_park_minor_policy.source: City of Chicago DCASE https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/dca/supp_info/millennium_park_visit.html (page published 16 Sep 2026)
millennium_park_minor_policy.discrepancy: CPD message relayed by CPS (30 Mar 2026) says 'Thursday through Sunday': https://www.cps.edu/media/community-updates/2026/march/youth-safety/ . Official DCASE page says Friday-Sunday. Use DCASE; flag the difference. Original policy introduced May 2022 (Lightfoot) https://www.fox32chicago.com/news/millennium-park-curfew-starts-thursday-unaccompanied-minors-no-longer-allowed-in-park-after-6-p-m (2022 version reported as weekday/weekend variants; current wording is from DCASE).

citywide_youth_curfew.rule: Age 12+: 10 p.m.; under 12: 8:30 p.m. (9 p.m. Fri-Sat); until 6 a.m.
citywide_youth_curfew.source: CPD youth-safety message via CPS, 30 Mar 2026 https://www.cps.edu/media/community-updates/2026/march/youth-safety/ (secondary relay; CPD original not fetched)

snap_curfew.2025: Council passed 'snap curfew' 27-22 on 18 Jun 2025 (Supt could declare curfews at short notice); Mayor Johnson vetoed; override failed in July 2025 - NOT law. https://www.fox32chicago.com/news/chicago-teen-curfew-vote-again ; https://blockclubchicago.org/2025/07/16/city-council-fails-to-override-mayor-brandon-johnsons-veto-of-controversial-snap-curfew-law/ (linked from Block Club; not fetched directly)
snap_curfew.2026: Hopkins' revised 'declaration of disruptive youth gathering' ordinance: committee approved a 12-hour-notice version 10-4 on 7 Jan 2026 (https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/01/07/city-council-public-safety-committee-revised-teen-curfew-measure), then held/watered down 21 Jan 2026. As of Block Club 28 May 2026 it was at an impasse with the Mayor's Office and not enacted: https://blockclubchicago.org/2026/05/28/teen-takeovers-revive-chicago-debate-over-curfews-and-parental-accountability/ . Parental Accountability Ordinance (fines $1,000-$10,000) rejected 16-32 on 17 Jun 2026 (CBS Chicago https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/revived-ordinance-penalize-parents-teen-takeovers-chicago/). Status after June 2026: NOT VERIFIED. Note: one WTTW summary (30 Mar 2026) implied a revised ordinance was passed and vetoed; contradicted by Block Club 28 May 2026 - treat as unverified/likely wrong.

downtown_measures.teen_takeover_events_2026: Late March 2026 Loop spring-break gathering: 8 arrests, 24 curfew violations (WTTW https://news.wttw.com/2026/03/30/teen-takeover-raises-questions-about-public-safety-spaces-young-people ). Memorial Day weekend 2026: 5 officers struck by a car on Near West Side (24 May); Hyde Park 3 shot, 53 arrested (Block Club 28 May 2026, URL above).

nov_2025_tree_lighting_shootings.date: Friday 21 Nov 2025 (evening of the Millennium Park Christmas tree lighting). Some outlets (CBS summary) wrongly say 22 Nov; Block Club published Sat 22 Nov and says 'Friday'.
nov_2025_tree_lighting_shootings.incident_1: About 9:40-9:50 p.m., 100-block N. State St by the Chicago Theatre (175 N. State): 7 teens (13-17) shot, non-fatal; one 17-year-old later charged as an adult (CPD https://www.chicagopolice.org/stories/dec-25-shooting-charges/ ; CBS https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/boy-17-charged-downtown-chicago-wounded-7-teens/ title only)
nov_2025_tree_lighting_shootings.incident_2: About 10:40 p.m., 100-block S. Dearborn St (Adams/Dearborn area per CBS): 14-year-old Armani Floyd killed; 18-year-old wounded, serious condition.
nov_2025_tree_lighting_shootings.context: Event advertised on social media as a 'teen takeover'; Mayor Johnson called them 'unauthorized events'; Ald. Hopkins alleged ~300 juveniles (his X post, unverified claim). CBS: 18 arrests, five guns recovered (not for the two shootings); $10,000 Crime Stoppers reward.
nov_2025_tree_lighting_shootings.follow_up: Downtown aldermen renewed curfew push 25 Nov 2025 https://blockclubchicago.org/2025/11/25/downtown-aldermen-renew-push-for-tougher-curfew-after-teen-takeover-shootings/ (headline only). 2026 tree lighting: Fri 20 Nov 2026 per DCASE; 2026 security plan NOT VERIFIED.

2025.aggravated_assaults_and_batteries: 469 in 2025 vs 441 in 2024, a 24-year high (CPD data via Sun-Times, 2 Mar 2026) https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2026/03/02/chicago-cta-transit-crime-assault-battery-leerhsen
2025.fta: FTA special directive 8 Dec 2025; CTA revised plan rejected 19 Dec 2025 as 'materially deficient'; up to $50m federal funding at risk; later deadline 19 Mar 2026 per Sun-Times (final outcome NOT VERIFIED).

2026.claims: CTA acting president Nora Leerhsen, 8 Jul 2026: June 2026 vs June 2025 system serious crime -45%, violent crime -58%; Red Line all crime -47%, serious -69%, violent -76%; six consecutive monthly declines (CBS Chicago https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/cta-says-crime-down-riders-dont-feel-safe/ ). WTTW 10 Jun 2026 (CPD data): most serious crimes -40% May25-May26; violent -20% YTD, property -35% YTD https://news.wttw.com/2026/06/10/cta-leaders-tout-ridership-gains-lower-crime-rates-system . Union leaders dispute the decline; Sun-Times 2 Mar 2026 reported violent crimes +33% in early 2026 vs 2025 (before the surge).
2026.measures: Security surge since March 2026: extra CPD and Cook County Sheriff patrols, esp. Red Line; new chief of security Joe Bird; bus/train ride-alongs; violence-intervention/crisis specialists planned; $54m extra rider-focused funding (WTTW, Sun-Times https://chicago.suntimes.com/transportation/2026/07/08/cta-transit-crime-security-surge ).

cta.caveat: Figures differ by metric (all/serious/violent/aggravated), period and source; CTA and CPD numbers are not directly comparable. Absolute 2026 counts NOT VERIFIED.

tap_to_pay_donation.what: Strangers claim to be raising money (often for a funeral), ask to 'tap' your phone/card for $10-$25 then charge thousands; refunds often refused as you authorised it.

reports.detail: Ald. Bennett Lawson warning; $5,000 loss; reports to 19th District https://cwbchicago.com/2025/08/alderman-warns-of-charity-donation-scam-operating-on-lakeview-streets.html (no CPD statement)
Attempt caught on video, no loss; CPD said it had no calls for service logged

$2,500-$3,000 charges; BBB Chicago president Steve Bernas quoted https://abc7chicago.com/post/chicago-crime-con-artists-claim-need-donations-kids-funerals-steal-thousands-tap-pay-ravenswood-lincoln-park/16273430/

tap_to_pay_donation.advice: Ask for a receipt, give cash or decline, never hand over/tap without seeing the amount, check bank statements (BBB via ABC7).
tap_to_pay_donation.official_cpd_warning: NOT VERIFIED - no CPD press release found; warnings are from BBB and an alderman via press.

fulton_market_fake_parking_attendants.source: Fulton Market Association via CBS Chicago https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/fulton-market-warning-fake-parking-attendants/
fulton_market_fake_parking_attendants.detail: People in yellow vests/security hats charging $20 to park in three private lots near Justine and Lake streets on weekends 9 p.m.-3 a.m. for about three months; association says 100+ drivers a night (association's estimate); advice: stay in car, lock doors, call police.
